faqs.q: Sec. 86-124. - Permanent; refusal to submit to reexamination.
faqs.a:
At least once each year for the first five years following the determination of permanent
               disability status under
section 86-156
and once in each three-year period thereafter, the board may require a disabled member,
               who has not attained the age of 55 years, to undergo a medical examination to be made
               by or under the direction of a physician designated by the board. Should any such
               disabled member refuse to submit to such medical examination upon request of the board,
               his disability pay may be discontinued by the board until such time as he shall submit
               to such examination, and should his refusal continue for one year, all his rights
               in and to disability pay and status may be revoked. If upon such medical examination
               of such disabled member, the physician certify to the board that such disabled member
               is physically able and capable of resuming employment in the service, the member shall
               be restored to service and the member's disability pay and status shall be terminated.
(Code 1960, § 19-13(B); Code 1981, § 26-59)
